Unit 2 — Education matters :رسﺪﻟا

Wael Academ
y
ةﻮﻄﺨﺑ ةﻮﻄﺧ ..ﻚﺘﯾاﺮﻗ ﻲﻓUNIT 2 Education matters
→ Fil unit hedhi bech na7kiw all virtual schools (yaani le9raya en ligne) w lifelong learning
(yaani le9raya mada al hayat), l unit hadhi tanajm tji fil writing ykolek a7kili al advantages w
drawbacks mtaa virtual schools wella y9olek a7kili aal lifelong learning wella l'importance
of education.
1. → Chnouwa hiyya l virtual schools? : online learning, e-learning, distance learning, cyber
school.
Advantages:
- No school uniforms, no heavy bags, no school journeys, no hustle and bustle (rushing);
(famech uniform lazem ennek telbsou, famech kartaba th9ila, famech 3outal, famech
hamajiyya).
- Virtual schools are an option for:
- Children who have been home-educated; (atfel 9raw fi dar yaani waldihom houma elli
9arawhom mamchewech l normal schools).
- Bullied children who need their confidence rebuilding; (atfel t3ardhou ll 3onf yhebou
y3awdou yebniw thi9a fi rwe7hom).
- Children with physical or personal health problems; (atfel 3andhom machakel jasadiyya
wella si7iyya).
Drawbacks:
Sitting long hours in front of the screen does have some side effects: (joulous barcha
9odem l checha mtaa l pc yaaml barcha adhrar janibiyya)
- No physical exercise or eye contact; (famech 7araka 9a3ed dima 9odem l pc w matchouf
had w lee had ychoufek).
- Little verbal and physical communication; (famech tawasol).
- No chance to learn how to handle the hustle and bustle and bullying in the society;
(maadekech forsa bech tel3alem kifech tetsaref m3a l fawdha w l hamajiyya w l3onf).
- Isolation, loneliness, no human relationships; (l we7da w maandekech 3ala9at m3a 3bed).

→ Bech nchoufou tawwa kifeh taamel GRAPH (rasm bayani) fih des pourcentages w enty
ta9rahom:
Fil graph nesta3mlou barcha "if, unlike, Unless"
If hiyaa idha w unlike hiyya mouch kif hakka l 7aja wella the place fiha mou9arna w unless = if
+ not
Example:
If we don't donate to UNICEF, children will not have a chance.
→ Idha manetbar3ouch ll UNICEF, sghar mouch bech tkoun 3andhom forsa.
Unless we donate to UNICEF, children will not have a chance.
→ Ella idha netbar3ou ll UNICEF, sghar mouch bech yal9aw forsa.
Example:
GRAPH
(l graph elli bech nekhdem alih mawjoud fil cours)
In this graph, we notice that South Asia suffers most from exclusion where there are 36% of
the children who don't go to school. This can be explained by the fact that people there are
very poor and don't believe in education.
Unlike South Asia, the percentage of the children who don't go to school in the
industrialized countries is very low as there are only 2.3% who are out of school. Here people
give much importance to the value of education.
The graph shows the distribution of children who don't attend school worldwide in the
academic year 2001/2002. The number of these children is approximately 115 million. More
than 40% of these came from Africa. Central Europe and industrialized countries suffer the
least from school absenteeism as only 4.8% of their children don't attend schools. The role
of UNICEF is vital in boosting school attendance. Donations can provide children with
school tools and recreation kits.
Vocabulary:
Break: pause
Bullying: frightening or hurting a weaker person
Log on: connect to a computer system
Appeal: what makes something attractive
Texting: writing on
Bustle: crowd of people moving in a busy way

To harass = to bother = to irritate = to annoy
Notes:
Sitting at a computer for 5 hours does have side effects
Do + infinitive without to
→ to emphasize the meaning
Online learning, like all learning, needs a lot of time commitment
→ An appositive clause
2. → Tawwa bech nahkiw aal lifelong learning yaani le9raya mada l 7ayet
Lifelong Learning is the concept that "it's never too soon or late for learning" (yaani enou
le9raya ma3andhech 3mor mou3ayn), that one can and should be open to new ideas,
decisions, opportunities or behaviours (enou nektachfou afkar jdod w nekhdhou 9ararat w
na3tiw fouras l rwe7na). Lifelong learning throws the axiom (rule, principle that people
believe to be true) "You can't teach an old dog new tricks" out the door (yaani enou w enty
kbir fil 3mor mouch bech tanf3ek le9raya). Lifelong learning sees citizens provided with
learning skills at all ages and in numerous contexts: at work, at home and through leisure
activities, not just through formal channels such as school and higher education.
Advantages:
- People will get totally involved in something that interests them. (bech ya3mlou haja
y7ebouha)
- People will see new ways of doing things. (bech yet3almou hajat jdida)
- People will no longer be ashamed of asking questions or volunteering for something new.
(mouch bech ye7chmou enhom yes2lou walla yetaw3ou bech yaamlou haja jdida)
- People will learn by talking with other people, exchanging opinions and experiences.
(bech yet3almou mn la7dith m3a 3bed okhra)
- People will try out new ideas or ways of working. (bech yjarbou touro9 jdida mtaa
khedma)
- People will learn to work well with others. (bech yet3almou kifeh yekhdmou maa abed
okhra)
Drawbacks:
- More important responsibilities such as family and job might be neglected. (ynajem
yohmel mas2ouliyatou kima l3ayla w lkhedma)

3. Exercise:
Reading:
The Text
1- Education is not merely preparation for an unknown kind of future living. The whole
of life is learning, therefore education can have no endings. This new venture is called
adult education not because it is confined to adults but because adulthood, maturity,
defines its limits. (……)
2- Education revolves about non-vocational ideals. Adult education more accurately
defined begins where vocational education leaves off. Its purpose is to put meaning
into the whole of life. (……)
3- The approach will be via the route of situations, not subjects. In conventional
education the student is required to adjust himself to an established curriculum; in
adult education the curriculum is built around the student's needs and interests. (……)
4- The resource of highest value in adult education is the learner's experience ….. all
genuine education will keep doing and thinking together. (……)
1) Read the text then match the titles to the corresponding paragraphs:
A. The learner's experience is paramount
B. Adult education should not be only professional
C. Education is for life
D. We should start with interests and needs
2) There are TWO different types of education mentioned in the text. What are they? Find
out the main differences between the two types.
→ Type one: ………………………………………………………………
Objective: It prepares students for a future living
Duration: Limited
Tools: ……………………………/……………………………

Paragraph about lifelong learning: (example of a body)
First, lifelong education is seen as building upon and affecting all existing educational
providers, including both schools and institutions of higher education. Second, key
features stand out of the accounts of lifelong education. Then, it extends beyond the
formal educational providers to encompass all agencies, groups and individuals
involved in any kind of learning activity. Last, it rests on the belief that individuals are,
or can become, self-directing, and they will see the value in engaging in lifelong
education.
More arguments about Lifelong Learning:
- Learning / education can have no endings.
- Adult education starts when professional learning stops.
- It's very important to engage ourselves in lifelong learning / adult education because it
updates our knowledge and enables us to do our jobs in a better way which is beneficial for
both people and country.
- Adult education is a very rewarding experience since it has a lot of benefits.
- In fact, it improves our memory, our self-confidence.

2. → Tawwa bech nahkiw aal lifelong learning yaani le9raya mada l 7ayet
Lifelong Learning is the concept that "it's never too soon or late for learning" (yaani enou
le9raya ma3andhech 3mor mou3ayn), that one can and should be open to new ideas,
decisions, opportunities or behaviours (enou nektachfou afkar jdod w nekhdhou 9ararat w
na3tiw fouras l rwe7na). Lifelong learning throws the axiom (rule, principle that people
believe to be true) "You can't teach an old dog new tricks" out the door (yaani enou w enty
kbir fil 3mor mouch bech tanf3ek le9raya). Lifelong learning sees citizens provided with
learning skills at all ages and in numerous contexts: at work, at home and through leisure
activities, not just through formal channels such as school and higher education.
Advantages:
- People will get totally involved in something that interests them. (bech ya3mlou haja
y7ebouha)
- People will see new ways of doing things. (bech yet3almou hajat jdida)
- People will no longer be ashamed of asking questions or volunteering for something new.
(mouch bech ye7chmou enhom yes2lou walla yetaw3ou bech yaamlou haja jdida)
- People will learn by talking with other people, exchanging opinions and experiences.
(bech yet3almou mn la7dith m3a 3bed okhra)
- People will try out new ideas or ways of working. (bech yjarbou touro9 jdida mtaa
khedma)
- People will learn to work well with others. (bech yet3almou kifeh yekhdmou maa abed
okhra)
Drawbacks:
- More important responsibilities such as family and job might be neglected. (ynajem
yohmel mas2ouliyatou kima l3ayla w lkhedma)

Paragraph about lifelong learning: (example of a body)
First, lifelong education is seen as building upon and affecting all existing educational
providers, including both schools and institutions of higher education. Second, key
features stand out of the accounts of lifelong education. Then, it extends beyond the
formal educational providers to encompass all agencies, groups and individuals
involved in any kind of learning activity. Last, it rests on the belief that individuals are,
or can become, self-directing, and they will see the value in engaging in lifelong
education.
More arguments about Lifelong Learning:
- Learning / education can have no endings.
- Adult education starts when professional learning stops.
- It's very important to engage ourselves in lifelong learning / adult education because it
updates our knowledge and enables us to do our jobs in a better way which is beneficial for
both people and country.
- Adult education is a very rewarding experience since it has a lot of benefits.
- In fact, it improves our memory, our self-confidence.
